papers.title: 3D bioprinting of collagen to rebuild components of the human heart.
papers.abstract: Collagen is the primary component of the extracellular matrix in the human body. It has proved challenging to fabricate collagen scaffolds capable of replicating the structure and function of tissues and organs. We present a method to 3D-bioprint collagen using freeform reversible embedding of suspended hydrogels (FRESH) to engineer components of the human heart at various scales, from capillaries to the full organ. Control of pH-driven gelation provides 20-micrometer filament resolution, a porous microstructure that enables rapid cellular infiltration and microvascularization, and mechanical strength for fabrication and perfusion of multiscale vasculature and tri-leaflet valves. We found that FRESH 3D-bioprinted hearts accurately reproduce patient-specific anatomical structure as determined by micro-computed tomography. Cardiac ventricles printed with human cardiomyocytes showed synchronized contractions, directional action potential propagation, and wall thickening up to 14% during peak systole.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文涉及3D生物打印胶原构建心脏组织，但完全没有使用人工智能技术。
llm.why_not_core: This paper describes a collagen bioprinting method without any integration of AI or machine learning into the bioprinting workflow.

summary_zh.motivation: 构建具有复杂结构和功能的心脏组织组件。
summary_zh.method: 利用FRESH技术3D生物打印胶原，通过pH控制凝胶化实现高分辨率。
summary_zh.result: 成功打印出心脏瓣膜、血管甚至完整心室，并观察到同步收缩。
summary_zh.validation: 显微CT验证解剖结构，心肌细胞收缩实验验证功能。

summary_en.motivation: To fabricate collagen scaffolds that replicate the structure and function of human heart components at multiple scales.
summary_en.method: FRESH 3D-bioprinting of collagen with pH-driven gelation to achieve 20-micrometer resolution and mechanical integrity for multiscale vasculature and valves.
summary_en.result: Printed heart structures including ventricles with human cardiomyocytes exhibited synchronized contractions and action potential propagation.
summary_en.validation: Micro-computed tomography confirmed anatomical accuracy, and functional tests demonstrated contractile behavior of printed cardiac tissue.

summary_zh.result: 提高了生物打印的结构保真度。

summary_en.motivation: To enable high-fidelity 3D bioprinting of soft materials such as hydrogels.
summary_en.method: The FRESH technique uses a thermoreversible support bath to embed printed filaments.
summary_en.result: The method achieves improved structural fidelity and enables printing of complex soft tissue constructs.
summary_en.validation: The approach was validated by printing cell-laden hydrogels and assessing viability and shape fidelity.
